headline: Chip crash drags stocks into correction
context: The S&P 500 fell every day and ended 10% below its record, as chip stocks had their worst week since 2001.

spx_days.label: Chip crash: S&P in a correction

winners.name: Tyson Foods
winners.why: Results beat forecasts on Monday, and it expects a much smaller beef loss next year.

winners.name: Hormel Foods
winners.why: No company news. Food makers were a safe place to hide as tech crashed (Tyson +10.7%).

winners.name: Palo Alto Networks
winners.why: Sales jumped 39% to $3.45B, beating forecasts, and it raised its full-year outlook.

winners.name: Tractor Supply
winners.why: No company news. Steadier, everyday-spending stocks held up as investors fled tech.

winners.name: Okta, Inc.
winners.why: Security stocks rallied after a string of outages, then on Palo Alto's strong results.

losers.name: Bloom Energy
losers.why: Its fuel cells power AI data centres, so it sank in the AI sell-off, falling 15% on Friday.

losers.name: Micron Technology
losers.why: Memory chips were hit hard as chip stocks had their worst week since 2001.

losers.name: Nvidia
losers.why: Sales doubled, but worries about its CEO's exit and an export probe outweighed the results.

losers.name: Lumentum
losers.why: Marvell is buying it with shares, so it fell with Marvell as chip stocks crashed.

losers.name: Freeport-McMoRan
losers.why: Copper miners all slumped on Wednesday (a typical drop of 8.6%), then fell with the market.

fun_fact.text: The S&P 500 fell all five days this week, four of them by 1% or more. Before now, that had only happened in 1962, 1974, 1978, after 9/11 and in October 2008.

watch.title: Dell results
watch.text: A read on demand for AI servers after this week's chip crash.

watch.title: Thanksgiving
watch.text: US markets closed. Friday is a half day, closing at 1pm New York time.
